title: Fire Technology
award: Certificate of Achievement requiring 16S/24Q to fewer than 30S/45Q units

program.section_heading: Fire Technology Certificate of Achievement and Associate in Science
outcomes: Identify and comprehend laws, regulations, codes and standards that influence fire department operations, and identify regulatory and advisory organizations that create and mandate them, especially in the areas of fire prevention, building codes and ordin
Analyze the causes of fire; determine extinguishing agents and methods; differentiate the stages of the fire and fire development; and compare methods of heat transfer.
Identify and describe common types of building construction and conditions associated with structural collapse and fire fighter safety.
Demonstrate the ability to analyze, appraise and evaluate fire and emergency incidents and identify components of emergency management and fire fighter safety.

notes: Read the 18-unit Fire Technology section (Certificate of Achievement and Associate in Science, catalog page 282), not the 40-unit Firefighter 1 & 2 Certificate of Achievement that follows it; the closed list and the 16-<30 unit award range match the 18-unit certificate.
The catalog prints codes with a leading zero (FIRE 050, 051, 053, 054, 056); these are matched to closed-list FIRE 50, 51, 53, 54, 56 and not flagged as catalog additions.

The PDF text has ligature extraction artifacts (e.g. 'IdenƟ fy', 'ﬁ re'); outcomes, careers and the heading were transcribed with those glyphs rendered as normal letters (ti, fi, fl, ff, ffi). A reviewer should check this against the PDF.
Program outcome 1 is cut off in the source text ('building codes and ordin'); recorded as printed, not completed.
The program outcomes list is shared by the Certificate of Achievement and the Associate in Science ('Fire Technology Certificate of Achievement/Associate in Science'); recorded for this certificate.
The 'minimum of 60 units' refers to the Associate in Science, not this certificate, so degree_total is null.
Careers 'engineer', 'captain', 'battalion chief' are ranks named for promotion of existing firefighters; 'fire service field' is named as a career field for non-safety employees.
